identity.title: To Grok Grokking: Provable Grokking in Ridge Regression

problem.claim: The paper studies grokking—the delayed onset of generalization after early overfitting—in over-parameterized ridge regression trained with gradient descent and weight decay.

gap.claim: The authors identify a lack of rigorous quantitative bounds relating generalization delay, or “grokking time,” to training hyperparameters.

contributions.claim: End-to-end results establish the sequential stages of overfitting, prolonged poor generalization, and eventual arbitrarily small generalization error in the linear setting.
The authors show that hyperparameter tuning can systematically amplify or eliminate grokking.
Experiments indicate that the quantitative bounds also capture grokking behavior in non-linear neural networks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their work provides the first rigorous quantitative bounds on grokking time in terms of training hyperparameters.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors prove that training first overfits, then remains poorly generalizing for an extended period, and eventually reaches arbitrarily small generalization error.
The authors report theoretical and empirical evidence that suitable hyperparameter choices can amplify or eliminate grokking.
The authors empirically report that their bounds capture grokking behavior in non-linear neural networks.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames grokking as delayed generalization after overfitting and studies it in ridge regression.
It proves the full overfit–delay–eventual-generalization sequence for over-parameterized linear regression with gradient descent and weight decay.
It reports that hyperparameter tuning can amplify or remove the phenomenon.

It states quantitative grokking-time bounds and tests their behavioral relevance on non-linear neural networks, motivating the view that grokking depends on training conditions rather than being inherent.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a staged theoretical account of the phenomenon with a controllability result and an empirical nonlinear extension.

lessons.interpretation: This links explanation, intervention, and scope extension in one compact argument.
lessons.application: When presenting a training pathology, define its temporal stages, identify controllable parameters, and test whether the explanation transfers beyond the simplest model.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the phenomenon is static, lacks measurable stages, or has no plausible intervention variable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the quantitative bounds, hyperparameter regimes, data assumptions, network architectures, or experimental protocols.
It does not report numerical effect sizes or define the conditions under which grokking is amplified or eliminated.
